chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Abū Ismāʿīl al-Sarrāj, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān, from Qudāmah ibn Abī Zayd al-Jammāl, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him: What is the minimum distance that should be between the well and the cesspit? He said: If it is soft ground, then seven cubits; and if it is rocky ground, then five cubits.

Then he said: Water flows toward the qiblah to the right, and it flows from the right of the qiblah to the left of the qiblah, and it flows from the left of the qiblah to the right of the qiblah, and it does not flow from the qiblah toward the rear of the qiblah.

key_terms.أَذْرُعٍ: cubits, a unit of distance measurement
key_terms.الْبَالُوعَةِ: the cesspit or drainage pit near which contamination is considered
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well from which water is drawn
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the qiblah, used here as a directional reference
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water, whose direction of flow affects the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum distance between a well and a cesspit in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the minimum distance between a well and a cesspit, distinguishing between soft land and rocky land. It also states directional principles regarding the flow of water, which are relevant to determining contamination and ritual purity in fiqh.
